Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 3,621 carloads, to 22,048; miscellaneous carloads, up 1,560 carloads, to 10,508; and motor vehicles and parts, up 1,405 carloads, to 16,320. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were coal, down 1,156 carloads, to 57,526; and farm products excl. grain, and food, down 1,009 carloads, to 16,863. candidates.title: Guangzhou and Hong Kong open electric container shuttle
candidates.excerpt: Guangzhou and Hong Kong open electric container shuttle Guangzhou Port has launched the Greater Bay Area’s first zero-carbon container route, putting a battery-electric vessel into cross-border service between Nansha and Hong Kong. The 240 teu Sui Gang Dian Hang 02 opened the route this week, carrying furniture and consumer goods to Hong Kong International Terminals. The vessel uses containerised batteries that can be exchanged by crane or recharged directly. An onboard platform monitors energy consumption, maintenance and ship-shore operations. Authorities estimate that each vessel in the series will eliminate more than 550 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually and over 19,000 tonnes during its operating life. No sailing frequency, cargo commitment or wider deployment schedule was disclosed.

Climbing intermodal rail volumes more than treble commodities traffic gains
candidates.excerpt: Freight of all kinds paced a 5% weekly gain among U.S. railroads from a year ago, according to the Association of American Railroads. For the week ending October 3, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 529,712 carloads and intermodal units, ahead 5.1% compared with the same week in 2025. A total of 230,711 carloads was better by 2.4% while intermodal volume was 299,001 containers and trailers, up 7.4% on 2025. Seven of 10 carload commodity groups tracked by AAR posted increases. They were topped by metallic ores and metals, 12.8%, closely followed by petroleum and related products, 12.2%. Forest products, which has mostly struggled in a stagnant housing market, took third, up 7.5%. Gran slipped 5.2%, while farm products excluding grain and food, 4.1%, and coal, 0.1%, were weaker y/y. Through the first 39 weeks of 2026, U.S. railroads reported cumulative volume of 8,910,593 carloads, a 2.7% gain, and 11,077,697 intermodal units, ahead 4.2% from the previous year.
